summary: Architecture phase determining how a verified governance methodology (GLP-001 v1.0, independently verified by Phase 137X) should itself be introduced into PCAE, using the same evidence-based discipline that produced it. Inventoried how every prior binding PCAE artifact (PFR-001, Canonical Phase ID Parsing Contract, Typed Authority Model Consumption Contract) was actually adopted, finding a consistent repository-native precedent: staged, prospective, never immediately mandatory. Independently evaluated five candidate adoption models (A Immediate Mandatory, B Mandatory-for-major-initiatives, C Advisory-first, D Pilot-based, E Opt-in) against proportionality, compatibility, incremental adoption, reversibility, and evidence-driven expansion; rejected Model A outright as contradicting both repository precedent and GLP-001's own designation-is-not-automatic text (GLP-REQ-003/014); found Models C, D, and E individually sound but incomplete alone. Recommended a six-stage evidence-gated adoption progression (Architecture available -> Contract verified -> Advisory use -> Pilot initiative -> Independent assessment -> Governance decision), with Stages 1-2 already satisfied as historical fact and Stages 3-6 explicitly not authorized by this phase. Designed a pilot architecture (candidate characteristics, success/evaluation/rollback/completion criteria) without running any pilot. Defined a compliance architecture that reuses existing per-stage phase-review mechanisms rather than introducing new GLP-specific tooling. Specified integration with existing governance surfaces (phase lifecycle, contracts, PFR-001, verification methodology, Typed Authority governance) as purely additive. Evaluated GLP-001 self-hosting (a graded citation-repair exception, one level of recursion, no meta-contract). Catalogued adoption-specific risks (governance inflation, ceremony, partial-adoption confusion, conflicting models, compliance ambiguity, pilot bias, overhead) with mitigations, defined adoption-process success metrics, and restated non-adoption criteria preserving proportionality. During this phase's own finalization, an independent bounded investigation (conducted at the user's explicit direction, not as part of this phase's substantive architecture) traced an initial validation-command discrepancy (99 apparent test failures under an unscoped 'full' pytest tier) to a documentation-consistency gap between CONTRIBUTING.md/bootstrap guidance and pyproject.toml's own fast-green/full tier distinction -- not a repository or governance regression. The correct fast-green-tier command reproduced 137V/137W/137X's exact baseline (4391 passed, 0 failed), confirming no defect blocks this phase's completion. This is disclosed as a single Non-Blocking finding (Section 17 of the architecture document) for future documentation correction; not repaired by this phase. No implementation. No governance behavior changes. No production code. No lifecycle enforcement introduced. No pilot run. Runtime remained Observed / observe / unavailable throughout.
